newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO UPS TOLLS ON FEDERAL GOVT HIGHWAYS, BRIDGES.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO UPS TOLLS ON FEDERAL GOVT HIGHWAYS, BRIDGES.

text.p: Mexico's government-run highway and bridge administrators said on Thursday they would raise toll fares next week by an average 5.6 percent.

The jump in tolls is the second this year, for a total 16.8 percent increase, the government body said in a statement. It said the hike would be applied on Aug. 11, and would be the final adjustment to tolls for the year.
The government's Caminos y Puentes administers tolls on 12 highways and 29 bridges.

Many of Mexico's freeways are operated by construction companies, which are suffering a big loss because of lower than expected traffic. A government aid program is expected to be announced in coming weeks.
Caminos y Puentes said the higher toll prices follows the rise in inflation. Accumulated inflation for the first seven months of the year was 9.61 percent, the Banco de Mexico said on Thursday.
